title: Clearing a Cache
fact_scope: DaVinci Resolve documents deleting unused, all, or selected render cache; original media is not affected and cache can be regenerated. It also identifies the project working-folder location and a separate cache volume as an optimization choice.
quality_note: First-party product documentation. It defines Resolve behavior, not independent user demand.

title: Project settings, caching, and preferences
fact_scope: Resolve offers smart and user cache modes, and cached clip data persists until changed or explicitly cleared. Cache is separate from the source timeline media.
quality_note: Older first-party documentation. Keep the fact narrow and re-check against the installed Resolve version before implementing an owner integration.

title: Clear media cache using preferences
fact_scope: Premiere exposes deletion of unused cache or all cache from its current location, and says deleted cache is recreated when source media requires it. Clearing all cache requires closing projects and choosing the action in Premiere settings.
quality_note: First-party product documentation updated in 2026. It defines the owner-app action and its precondition, not a generic filesystem rule.

title: Manage media cache
fact_scope: Premiere media cache contains accelerator files and a cache database, can be cleared regularly, and can be placed on a fast dedicated drive.
quality_note: First-party product documentation updated in 2026. Use it to identify cache ownership and location, not to infer that every Adobe-owned file is removable.

title: Manage render files in Final Cut Pro for Mac
fact_scope: Final Cut Pro stores render files in a library or external location, and offers deletion of unused or all generated render files at project, event, or library scope. Original media is not deleted and render files can be regenerated.
quality_note: First-party product documentation. The scope selector matters because library-wide deletion differs from selected-project cleanup.

title: Create optimized and proxy files in Final Cut Pro for Mac
fact_scope: Final Cut Pro can delete optimized or proxy media for selected clips, projects, events, or libraries while retaining original media. Some generated-file commands also affect external media, so scope must be shown.
quality_note: First-party product documentation. External-media impact is a material warning for a cross-app cleanup tool.

title: What are libraries in Final Cut Pro for Mac?
fact_scope: Final Cut Pro libraries can contain managed media, while external media remains outside the library. Generated render, optimized, proxy, and analysis files may be stored inside or outside the library and can be removed to reduce library size.
quality_note: First-party product documentation. It establishes why a library package cannot be judged by size alone.

title: Free up space with online-only files
fact_scope: Dropbox distinguishes online-only files from available-offline files. Its Manage hard drive space tool sorts by size or modification time, confirms the amount freed, and changes local availability without deleting the cloud item. Deleting an online-only file deletes it everywhere in Dropbox.
quality_note: First-party Dropbox documentation updated in 2025. It defines the provider action boundary and the logical-versus-physical size issue.

title: Dropbox support for macOS File Provider
fact_scope: Dropbox documents its macOS File Provider integration and the platform requirements that affect how Dropbox files appear and behave in Finder. Provider integration and macOS version therefore belong in the detected ownership context.
quality_note: First-party Dropbox platform documentation. Treat behavior as version-sensitive and verify the installed provider state before action.

title: Save disk space with OneDrive Files On-Demand for Mac
fact_scope: OneDrive distinguishes online-only, locally available, and always-available states. Opening an online-only file downloads it; Free up space makes it online-only without deleting it from OneDrive. Deleting an online-only file deletes it from OneDrive on all devices, while the web recycle bin can restore it for a limited period.
quality_note: First-party Microsoft documentation. The state icon and provider action must be shown separately from a generic file delete.

title: Stream and mirror files with Drive for desktop
fact_scope: Google Drive separates streaming, where files are primarily cloud-backed and local cache is used, from mirroring, where a full local copy is kept. Switching modes requires completed sync and can change local paths, while extensive writing, video editing, and high-resolution photo editing may favor mirroring.
quality_note: First-party Google documentation. The mode and sync completion state are required before suggesting local cleanup or folder removal.

title: Work with folders and files in iCloud Drive
fact_scope: Apple documents iCloud Drive status indicators and the Finder action Remove Download when the user wants to remove a local download while keeping the iCloud Drive item. The action is distinct from deleting the item from iCloud Drive.
quality_note: First-party Apple Mac User Guide. The visible status and exact action should be used to prevent a generic delete from becoming a remote delete.

title: Locate and manage backups of your iPhone, iPad, and iPod touch
fact_scope: Apple documents the local iPhone or iPad backup path and the Finder Manage Backups control. The owner UI can delete, archive, or reveal a backup, so a backup path needs device identity and owner-managed handling.
quality_note: First-party Apple support guidance published in 2026. It defines the backup owner and actions, not user demand or proof that an arbitrary backup is disposable.

title: Back up your Mac with Time Machine
fact_scope: Apple documents that Time Machine keeps older versions, automatically removes older backups when the backup disk is full, and is best used with a dedicated backup disk. It also defines restore as the purpose of the data.
quality_note: First-party Apple support guidance published in 2026. Use it to explain history and restore value, not to assume automatic pruning succeeded in the current incident.

title: FAQs for Docker Desktop for Mac
fact_scope: Docker Desktop for Mac stores Linux containers and images in a large disk image. Docker documents that the file can show a maximum or sparse size different from actual use, that cleanup should use Docker controls, and that reducing the maximum size can delete the current image and its contents.
quality_note: First-party Docker documentation. It defines the owner-managed disk image and the destructive boundary around changing its maximum size.

title: Prune unused Docker objects
fact_scope: Docker documents separate prune operations for stopped containers, unused networks, dangling or unused images, build cache, and volumes. Volumes need explicit treatment because they may contain persistent data.
quality_note: First-party Docker documentation. The separate commands support narrow, owner-aware actions instead of deleting Docker's disk image as a generic file.

title: Back up and restore Docker Desktop
fact_scope: Docker documents backing up Docker.raw only after Docker Desktop is stopped, and notes that containers, images, and volumes need appropriate backup handling. Restore uses the Docker-managed location.
quality_note: First-party Docker documentation. It defines recovery prerequisites for the owner-managed image and prevents a scanner from presenting raw-file deletion as a normal cleanup action.

title: Docker Desktop settings
fact_scope: Docker Desktop exposes a disk usage limit and a disk image location in its settings. The location should be moved through Docker's settings rather than by moving the image file in Finder.
quality_note: First-party Docker documentation. Treat the configured owner location and the UI-reported usage as current state that can change between scans.

title: Resize and compress a UTM drive
fact_scope: UTM documents reclaiming or compressing a disk image after the guest is shut down and unused blocks are released. It marks the operation as experimental and recommends backing up the VM first.
quality_note: First-party UTM documentation. The shutdown, TRIM, backup, and experimental-status conditions are hard gates for any future source-aware action.

title: UTM drive settings
fact_scope: UTM documents removable and non-removable drives, drive locations, sparse images on APFS, and the different deletion consequences for attached drives. A non-removable drive deletion deletes its data.
quality_note: First-party UTM documentation. It supports distinguishing a VM bundle, an attached data drive, and an image's apparent size before any action.

title: Back up Windows with Time Machine
fact_scope: Parallels documents SmartGuard snapshots, a maximum snapshot count, replacement of the oldest snapshot at the limit, and an Optimize for Time Machine mode that backs up the latest snapshot instead of the whole virtual machine.
quality_note: First-party Parallels guidance last reviewed in 2021. Use as version-sensitive owner context and verify the installed Parallels version before relying on its settings.

title: Working with snapshots in Parallels Desktop for Mac
fact_scope: Parallels defines a snapshot as saved VM state, allows restore and deletion through Snapshot Manager, merges data when an intermediate snapshot is deleted, and disallows compressing or resizing a virtual disk while snapshots exist.
quality_note: First-party Parallels guidance last reviewed in 2024. Snapshot deletion changes a chain of VM state and must remain owner-managed.

title: Fix not enough disk space to start a Windows virtual machine
fact_scope: Parallels explains that the host macOS drive can block VM startup, recommends checking host available space, and notes that free host space may need to match the VM memory allocation. It points to snapshot cleanup only as an optional owner action.
quality_note: First-party Parallels guidance last reviewed in 2023. It supports showing host and guest resource demands separately.

title: Free up disk space on Mac
fact_scope: Parallels documents freeing space inside the guest, reclaiming unused virtual disk space after shutdown, deleting unneeded snapshots, and archiving an infrequently used VM. It warns not to terminate the VM during reclaim and notes that snapshot branches can change the result.
quality_note: First-party Parallels guidance last reviewed in 2022. The shutdown, snapshot, archive, and reclaim steps are owner actions, not generic file cleanup.

title: How to reclaim virtual machine hard disk space
fact_scope: Parallels exposes a Reclaim action in the VM configuration and asks for confirmation. The action targets unused virtual hard disk space and is distinct from deleting the VM bundle.
quality_note: First-party Parallels guidance last reviewed in 2019. Keep it as historical owner evidence and validate behavior against the installed version.
